numerical_characteristics.magnitude: int64.min (the NaT sentinel) for integer-encoded time arrays; values outside the int64 range raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta
category_specific_evidence: Integer-encoded NaT is the int64.min sentinel (numpy/pandas NaT bit pattern); float-encoded NaT is NaN (passage: _decode_to_timedelta comment and code checking value.dtype.kind == 'i' and int(value) == np.iinfo('int64').min, or kind == 'f' and np.isnan(value)).
Correct handling: both int64.min and float NaN return np.timedelta64('NaT', unit) before the multiplication; decode_cf-level callers then return pd.Timestamp('NaT') for NaT dates.
Under numpy >= 2.5 (numpy/numpy#31378), int64.min * timedelta64 raises OverflowError instead of silently producing NaT, which is the root cause of the regression.
Values greater than int64 max or less than int64 min raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta.
Before the fix, unsigned dtype overflow was checked via np.int64(delta) == value and raised OutOfBoundsTimedelta; this was removed in the diff.
Infinity handling, signed zero and subnormals are not mentioned in the passages.
Regression coverage is said to exist via int64.min parametrizations of test_cf_timedelta and test_roundtrip_timedelta64_nanosecond_precision.
Test parametrize change pins np.datetime64 to ns unit to avoid DeprecationWarning for the unitless generic dtype under numpy >= 2.5 (not a numerical value issue but collection-related).
reproduction_risks: The NaT detection uses int(value) on int64 inputs; reproduction must use int64 dtype with exact int64.min value, not a float approximation.
Behavior depends on numpy version (>= 2.5 raises OverflowError on int64.min * timedelta64); on older numpy the multiplication silently yields NaT.
Passages do not state whether unsigned dtypes with int64.min trigger the same path.
